teaser.text: Pembina Pipeline is a midstream energy company: it connects wells to products, markets and customers. Its dollar comes in through infrastructure services and commodity sales, then goes out through the costs of running, maintaining, financing and expanding that network.

stock.title: Pembina stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Pembina's stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios against cash flow, project execution, financing and valuation.
stock.opening: The weighted price reaches C$69.64 by October 2027 and C$78.69 by October 2029. The outcome hinges on fee-based growth, Cedar’s execution and financing, and marketing earnings.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Pembina’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

paragraphs.text: Pembina’s weighted outcome is modest in the first year but improves as Cedar and fee-based growth contribute. The starting price is C$69.63. The weighted price reaches C$69.64 by October 2027, a 4% return including dividends. It reaches C$72.11 by October 2028, a 12% return. By October 2029, it reaches C$78.69, a 26% return.
The three-year range is wide: C$35.08 in the bear case to C$122.52 in the bull case. The weighted forecast assigns 30% to the bear, 55% to the base and 15% to the bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Pembina?

paragraphs.text: The view would move toward the bear case if marketing spreads weaken from late 2026 onward. Lower Marketing & New Ventures EBITDA would reduce both earnings and the multiple. blocks.heading: How much cash does Pembina really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow needs a careful bridge. Start with operating cash, then deduct capital spending, lease payments and the additional interest paid during construction. Most cash interest has already passed through operating cash flow, so deducting it again would count it twice. Stock-based compensation can then be treated as an economic cost to shareholders, even though its cash settlement is already reflected in the cash-flow statement.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Pembina?

paragraphs.text: The dividend still competes with maintenance, interest and construction spending. Pembina’s free-cash-flow definition subtracts dividends, capital spending and contributions to equity-accounted ventures from operating cash flow. It reported C$335 million of free cash flow for 2025, but expected a deficit in 2026 as Cedar LNG reaches its largest investment year. The valuation therefore leads naturally to the question of whether today’s price is expensive relative to Pembina’s own past.

dividend.title: Pembina dividend: yield, history and cash cover
dividend.meta_description: Pembina pays $0.735 quarterly, with a 4.2% yield and roughly C$335 million left in 2025 after dividends, capital spending and investee contributions.
dividend.opening: Pembina pays $0.735 a share quarterly; in 2025, operating cash after dividends left C$1,529 million, and after capital spending and investee contributions roughly C$335 million remained. That is cash coverage after those listed needs, but the remaining dividend test also includes maintenance, preferred dividends, leases and joint-venture commitments.
dividend.closing: The full Pembina memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Pembina pay shareholders over time?

paragraphs.text: Dividends remained the dependable capital return. Buybacks peaked at $333 million in 2022 but were zero in both 2024 and 2025. Pembina later authorized purchases of up to 5% of its shares, but authorization is not spending. It also raised the quarterly dividend approximately 3.5% to $0.735 a share, adding a recurring claim on future cash.

paragraphs.subsection: 5.8 — Capital needs, debt and cash for shareholders
paragraphs.text: The bridge narrows after investment. Operating cash less those dividends left C$1,529 million before capital spending. Deducting C$784 million of capital expenditure and C$410 million of contributions to equity-accounted investees left roughly C$335 million before other uses. The company’s own free-cash-flow definition also starts after dividends and includes investee contributions, so identically named measures can answer different questions.

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from C$3.00 to C$3.18 per share. The bear case freezes the current C$2.94 run rate, while the bull case reaches C$3.28. The latest annual dividend was C$2.82 and the stated quarterly rate implies C$2.94 annually. The base therefore continues the steady increase in the supplied history, but remains below the earnings-growth target because construction and leverage constrain distributions.

The view would move toward the bear case if marketing spreads weaken from late 2026 onward. Lower Marketing & New Ventures EBITDA would reduce both earnings and the multiple. Cedar commissioning delays or cost overruns during 2027–2029 would add debt before contracted cash flow arrives. Higher refinancing costs or partnership debt would further reduce cash available for dividends and buybacks.

blocks.heading: What is Pembina's dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: The dividend tells the same story from another angle. In a simple constant-growth model, the current 4.2% yield implies about 5.8% annual dividend growth when an investor requires a 10% return. At a 9% required return, the implied growth falls to about 4.8%. The price does not reveal one unique growth expectation because the answer depends on both the return demanded and the length of the growth period.

earnings.title: Pembina earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Pembina's next results are expected on November 5, 2026; guidance is C$4,350 million–C$4,550 million, with marketing and project milestones to watch.
earnings.opening: Pembina's next results are expected on November 5, 2026. Watch whether marketing strength persists and whether new assets are supplying fee income.
earnings.closing: The full Pembina memo also answers questions about its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to adjusted EBITDA of C$4,350 million–C$4,550 million for 2026 and is tracking toward the midpoint. Adjusted EBITDA is an operating scoreboard before interest, taxes, depreciation and selected adjustments. It helps compare operations, but it is not cash available for dividends or construction.

Beneath it, management expects about 4.0% fee-based EBITDA growth in 2026 and about 5.0% annual growth per share through 2026. The longer target is 5.0%–7.0% annual fee-based EBITDA-per-share growth through 2030. Per share matters because new shares can increase total earnings while reducing each existing owner’s portion.

blocks.heading: Has Pembina kept its project promises?

paragraphs.text: Execution supplies a more visible test. Pembina said its Redwater fractionation expansion entered service in May and its Wapiti expansion in March, both on time and at or below budget. That supports management’s record of completing projects, but it does not prove that every project will earn its expected return.

blocks.heading: How have Pembina's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: Revenue, operating income, net income and diluted EPS all increased year over year, while gross margin was nearly unchanged. The business therefore earned more gross profit mainly on a larger base, not because consolidated margins suddenly widened.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Pembina's next results?

paragraphs.text: Cedar targets mechanical completion by the end of 2027, vessel arrival in the first half of 2028 and service in late 2028. Heartland follows in late 2029, then Greenlight in the second half of 2030. Delays can defer revenue while construction interest continues.
